content.key_idea: CENT implements tensor parallelism by spreading each transformer decoder block's fully-connected layers across all CXL devices via broadcast/gather over the CXL switch, while keeping the infrequent, communication-heavy residual/normalization and attention layers on a single master device to avoid expensive AllReduce overhead.
content.reading_order: Left panel (a): decoder blocks are processed sequentially, one at a time, across all CXL devices for a single prompt; right panel (b): a zoom into one decoder block, color-coding which layers stay on a single device versus which are broadcast/gathered across multiple devices.

summary: Figure 9 shows how CENT maps tensor parallelism (TP) across its CXL devices. Panel (a) shows the host dispatching decoder blocks through the CXL switch to all CXL devices, with Decoder 0, Decoder 1, and Decoder 2 processed sequentially over time for a single prompt. Panel (b) zooms into one decoder block: fully-connected layers (green) are spread across multiple CXL devices via broadcast and gather operations over the CXL switch (each moving 16KB), while Add & Norm, the attention-score computation, and SiLU (blue) are confined to a single master CXL device because distributing attention would require costly AllReduce communication. The figure uses a simple color legend to mark single-device versus multi-device layer placement.
summary_zh: 图9展示CENT的张量并行映射：(a) 主机通过CXL交换机将解码器块依次分发给所有CXL设备，单个提示下Decoder 0/1/2按时间顺序处理；(b) 放大单个解码器块，全连接层（绿色）通过广播/收集跨多设备分布，而Add & Norm、注意力分数和SiLU（蓝色）因AllReduce通信开销大而固定在单一主设备上。
